title: Showing Concern
subtitle: စိတ်ပူကြောင်း ပြောခြင်း
review: Written by Claude. The Burmese lines are drafts: check every one before publishing or recording.

categories.my: ဘာဖြစ်လို့လဲ မေးခြင်း
categories.desc: The first questions when someone looks hurt, sad or upset.
cards: Are you okay?
အဆင်ပြေရဲ့လား။
The first question to ask. Also: Are you all right?
You fell! Are you okay?
လဲကျသွားတာပဲ။ အဆင်ပြေရဲ့လား။
What's wrong?
Asks gently what the problem is.
You're not eating. What's wrong?
ထမင်းမစားဘူးနော်။ ဘာဖြစ်လို့လဲ။
What's the matter?
ဘာဖြစ်တာလဲ။
The same meaning as What's wrong?, a little softer.
You look sad. What's the matter?
ဝမ်းနည်းနေပုံပဲ။ ဘာဖြစ်တာလဲ။
What happened?
ဘာဖြစ်ခဲ့တာလဲ။
Asks about something that is finished: an accident, a fall, bad news.
Your knee is bleeding! What happened?
ဒူးက သွေးထွက်နေတယ်။ ဘာဖြစ်ခဲ့တာလဲ။
Is everything all right?
Polite. Good for people you do not know well.
You left early yesterday. Is everything all right?

categories.my: သတိထားမိတာကို ပြောခြင်း
categories.desc: Telling someone, kindly, that you can see something is not right.
cards: You look tired.
ပင်ပန်းနေပုံပဲ။
You look + adjective: tired, sad, pale, worried. Not: You look tiredly.
You look tired. Did you sleep well?
ပင်ပန်းနေပုံပဲ။ ကောင်းကောင်း အိပ်ရရဲ့လား။
You don't look well.
Well here means healthy.
You don't look well. Do you want to go home?
နေမကောင်းတဲ့ပုံပဲ။ အိမ်ပြန်ချင်လား။
Are you sure?
Ask again when someone says I'm fine but does not look fine.
“I'm fine.” “Are you sure? You're very quiet.”
“အဆင်ပြေပါတယ်။” “သေချာလား။ အရမ်း တိတ်နေတယ်နော်။”
Is something bothering you?
တစ်ခုခု စိတ်ပူစရာ ရှိလား။
Bother: to make someone worried or unhappy.
You keep looking at your phone. Is something bothering you?
ဖုန်းကိုပဲ ခဏခဏ ကြည့်နေတယ်။ တစ်ခုခု စိတ်ပူစရာ ရှိလား။
Does it hurt?
For the body: a cut, a fall, a headache.
You hit your head. Does it hurt?

categories.my: တစ်ယောက်ယောက်အတွက် စိတ်ပူခြင်း
categories.desc: When you do not know if a person is safe or well.
cards: I'm worried about you.
မင်းအတွက် စိတ်ပူတယ်။
Worried about + a person or a thing.
You work too much. I'm worried about you.
မင်း အလုပ်တွေ အရမ်းလုပ်တယ်။ မင်းအတွက် စိတ်ပူတယ်။
I was so worried!
အရမ်း စိတ်ပူနေတာ။
Said when the person is back, or safe at last.
You're home! I was so worried!
ပြန်ရောက်ပြီပဲ။ အရမ်း စိတ်ပူနေတာ။
What if he's sick?
သူ နေမကောင်းဖြစ်နေရင်ကော။
What if…? imagines something bad that is possible.
She's not answering. What if she's lost?
သူ ဖုန်းမကိုင်ဘူး။ လမ်းပျောက်နေရင်ကော။
I hope everything's okay.
အားလုံး အဆင်ပြေပါစေ။
Kind to say or write when you do not know yet.
I heard about your mother. I hope everything's okay.
မင်းအမေအကြောင်း ကြားတယ်။ အားလုံး အဆင်ပြေပါစေ။
That's a relief!
Said when the worry is over.
“The doctor says it's nothing.” “That's a relief!”
“ဆရာဝန်က ဘာမှ မဖြစ်ဘူးတဲ့။” “စိတ်အေးသွားပြီ။”

categories.my: ဂရုစိုက်ကြောင်း ပြခြင်း
categories.desc: What to say when you hear bad news, big or small.
cards: Oh no!
ဟာ၊ ဒုက္ခပါပဲ။
The natural first reaction to bad news.
“I lost my wallet.” “Oh no!”
Poor thing!
သနားစရာလေး။
Warm and informal: for a friend, a child, an animal. Not for your boss.
“She has a fever.” “Poor thing!”
That's terrible.
For serious bad news. Also: That's awful.
“Someone stole her bike.” “That's terrible.”
Can I do anything?
ဘာကူညီပေးရမလဲ။
Offers help without pushing. Also: Is there anything I can do?
You look so tired. Can I do anything?
အရမ်း ပင်ပန်းနေပုံပဲ။ ဘာကူညီပေးရမလဲ။
Take care of yourself.
Said to someone who is sick, tired or sad, often when you say goodbye.
Get some rest. Take care of yourself.

categories.my: ပြန်ဖြေခြင်း
categories.desc: What to say when someone is worried about you.
cards: I'm fine.
အဆင်ပြေပါတယ်။
The usual answer, even when it is not completely true.
“Are you okay?” “I'm fine. Just tired.”
“အဆင်ပြေရဲ့လား။” “အဆင်ပြေပါတယ်။ ပင်ပန်းနေရုံပါ။”
It's nothing.
ဘာမှ မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။
It is not serious.
“You're bleeding!” “It's nothing. Just a small cut.”
“သွေးထွက်နေတယ်။” “ဘာမှ မဟုတ်ပါဘူး။ နည်းနည်း ရှမိတာပါ။”
Don't worry.
စိတ်မပူပါနဲ့။
Tells the other person to stop worrying. Also: Don't worry about me.
Don't worry. I'll call you when I arrive.
စိတ်မပူပါနဲ့။ ရောက်ရင် ဖုန်းဆက်မယ်။
Thanks for asking.
A polite way to end your answer.
I'm much better now. Thanks for asking.
